difficultyRationale: Tests whether the candidate understands that bean scope, not just class design, decides whether mutable instance state is safe to use.
prompt: A bean is defined with the default scope and has a mutable, non-thread-safe instance field that accumulates per-request data (e.g. `private final List<String> items = new ArrayList<>();`, appended to on every call). Under load from many concurrent requests, this causes data from one request to leak into another's results. What is the most direct fix that addresses the actual cause without assuming a new Spring bean is created for every HTTP request?
explanation: Spring's default singleton scope shares one bean instance per application context, so a mutable list stored as a singleton field is shared across requests. The simplest fix is to keep the per-call accumulator in a method-local variable or parameter. When per-request bean state is genuinely needed, use an appropriate web request scope. Prototype scope creates a new instance on each container lookup/injection, **not** automatically per HTTP request; if a prototype is injected into a singleton just once, that same injected instance remains in the singleton. To obtain multiple prototypes dynamically, explicitly look them up (for example with ObjectProvider) or use an appropriate method-injection mechanism. Synchronization or a concurrent list can address data races but does not isolate each request's results.

options.text: Add `synchronized` to the methods that read and write `items`, which serializes concurrent access to the list so no two threads ever mutate it at the same instant.
options.explanation: Synchronizing prevents a torn/corrupted list under concurrent writes, but every request still shares the same `items` list, so one request's accumulated data still shows up in another's results — the leakage, not just the race, is the reported bug.

options.text: Mark the field `volatile` so each thread sees the latest write to it instead of a stale, thread-local cached copy left over from an earlier read.
options.explanation: `volatile` only affects visibility of the field reference itself, not the fact that a single shared `ArrayList` instance is being mutated by every request; it does nothing to stop the cross-request leakage.

options.text: Remove the per-request accumulator from the shared singleton field and make it a method-local value (or use properly isolated request-scoped state); only use prototype scope if a fresh instance is explicitly obtained per use.
options.explanation: Correct: local or genuinely request-scoped state prevents different requests from sharing one mutable list. Prototype means a new bean upon lookup/injection, not automatically one bean per HTTP request; injecting a prototype directly into a singleton once does not refresh it on each call.

options.text: Switch the field's type from `ArrayList` to `CopyOnWriteArrayList`, which snapshots the backing array on every write so readers never observe a partially-updated list.
options.explanation: A thread-safe collection type prevents concurrent-modification corruption of the list itself, but all requests would still read and write the same shared list, so data still leaks between unrelated requests.
